metaDescription: Own mineral rights in South Waverly, right on the New York line? We buy Bradford County Marcellus interests directly and pay cash.
heroLead: South Waverly sits so close to the New York border that half the families here have relatives who leased land on the New York side too, where drilling has been effectively banned for over a decade, which makes the difference across that line feel personal.
intro: South Waverly is a small borough in Bradford County, right on the New York state line across from Waverly, New York, in the dry-gas Marcellus fairway that made Bradford County one of the most productive counties in the entire play. Chesapeake Energy built a large early position across this county, and while ownership of some of those assets has since changed hands, the wells themselves have kept producing for well over a decade in many cases.

Because New York State has maintained a ban on high-volume hydraulic fracturing since 2014, families here often have a front-row view of just how different the two states' approaches turned out, watching development continue steadily on the Pennsylvania side while it never started across the line.

sections.heading: Living Right on the Line Between Two Different States' Rules
paragraphs: Pennsylvania's rules, including the Guaranteed Minimum Royalty Act and the case law around post-production deductions, apply fully to any interest located in South Waverly or the surrounding Bradford County townships. If your family also has land or relatives just across the border in New York, it's worth knowing those two properties are governed by entirely different legal frameworks, even though they might sit within sight of each other.

sections.heading: What Long-Producing Bradford County Units Are Worth
paragraphs: Because a lot of wells in this part of Bradford County have been producing for well over a decade, we can often value your interest against real, extended production history rather than a projection. We check current unit status, review any statements you have, and give you a clear cash offer.

faqs.question: My family also owns land just across the border in New York. Does that affect my Pennsylvania minerals?
faqs.answer: No. Your Pennsylvania interest is governed entirely by Pennsylvania law regardless of what rules apply to property across the state line.

faqs.question: Why is Bradford County considered one of the most productive Marcellus counties?
faqs.answer: Early, extensive leasing combined with strong dry-gas production from operators like Chesapeake Energy made this one of the most heavily developed parts of the play, and many of those original wells are still producing today.

faqs.question: How do I know if my original operator has changed since my lease was signed?
faqs.answer: Assignments of oil and gas leases get recorded at the Bradford County recorder of deeds. We can research the current operator and confirm who's actually responsible for your royalty payments.
